subject: Clarify DPA notification window & subprocessor cooperation — Finex Systems
messages:
From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@finex.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA — notification timing + subprocessor cooperation questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for stepping in. As we review the draft DPA our legal and InfoSec teams flagged two items we need clarified before procurement can move forward:

1) Notification window: the draft says "prompt notice" and "as soon as reasonably possible" — we need a concrete maximum window for incidents affecting Finex customer data (preferably an explicit 72-hour maximum for material breaches, with interim status updates).

2) Subprocessor cooperation: if the incident originates in a Redwood subprocessor (or a cross-border subprocess), we need a specified cooperation commitment — e.g., forensic evidence access within X business days, preserved logs, and a named technical liaison. Also want a statement about cross-border transfer assistance (if evidence resides in EU/APAC).

Can you confirm Redwood's committed timelines and whether you can accept explicit language or will propose a compromise redline? Procurement expects answers by end of day Wednesday to stay on our quarter cadence.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Security Ops, Finex Systems

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@finex.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — notification timing + subprocessor cooperation questions

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (sales/legal liaison) and Marissa (privacy ops) to give a consolidated reply and proposed language. High level: Redwood can commit to an operational timeline and a cooperation playbook, but we usually avoid hard-coded multi-jurisdictional transfer promises in the DPA — we can, however, commit to defined response SLAs and an evidence-handback process.

Next steps from our side:
- Ben to review procurement ask on the 72-hour hard cap and propose an alternative clause.
- Marissa to provide an internal runbook summary for subprocessor-origin incidents (forensic access, log preservation, liaison).
- I will confirm escalation points and point people.

We should be able to give you a redline and a short runbook by COB Wednesday. If procurement needs something sooner for signature sequencing, flag that and we can prioritize.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Alex Geller <alex.geller@finex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-09T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — notification timing + subprocessor cooperation questions

Alex / Rishi — quick note from Contracts/Sales perspective. We typically resist hard 72-hour contractual caps for all incident classes because escalation windows vary by severity and investigation needs. Two pragmatic proposals:

Option A (preferred): Commit to initial notification within 24 hours of becoming aware for incidents meeting our materiality threshold, with a contractual maximum of 96 hours for full notification details if ongoing triage is blocking completeness. Commit to daily status updates until closure.

Option B (customer concession): Accept a 72-hour maximum for notification but with carve-outs for situations requiring law enforcement coordination or active, time-bound forensic containment (must notify within 24 hours that the 72-hour clock is paused and why).

On subprocessor cooperation: Redwood will commit to a documented cooperation plan backed by SLAs:
- Forensic evidence handover (hashes, logs, timelines) within 5 business days after evidence collection is authorized by both parties' legal teams;
- Named technical liaison reachable within 4 hours for severity 1 incidents (business hours) and 12 hours off-hours;
- Where data/evidence resides in a different region, Redwood will assist with lawful transfer requests and coordinate with subprocessors to provide copies or extracts necessary for Finex's investigation, subject to applicable law.

I'll draft contract language for either Option A or B and Marissa can vet the runbook wording. Let me know which you'd prefer us to redline against.

– Ben
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: suggested-notify-clause.txt (inline suggestions)

From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@finex.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finex.com
Date: 2026-05-10T08:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — notification timing + subprocessor cooperation questions

Ben / Rishi — thanks, that helps. Procurement prefers Option A with the 96-hour maximum instead of open-ended "as soon as reasonably possible" language. They also want the forensic handover SLA tightened to 3 business days where evidence is not subject to third-party legal restrictions. Procurement will accept a 5 business day SLA only if there's written justification tied to data residency or legal hold.

Two procurement asks to surface now:
- Can you add a clause that Redwood will list relevant subprocessors with contact liaisons when an incident involves subprocessors?
- Will Redwood accept a clause allowing Finex to request a limited export of relevant logs/copies for investigation if Redwood's subprocessor won't provide timely access (Redwood to facilitate or provide redacted extracts)?

We need to factor these asks into the redline so procurement can align with legal.

Alex

---

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Alex Geller <alex.geller@finex.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — notification timing + subprocessor cooperation questions

Alex — attached are two things: (1) a compact "incident cooperation appendix" that spells out liaison roles, escalation matrices, and the evidence-handback checklist; (2) a suggested redline that implements Option A with a 96-hour hard maximum for provision of consolidated notification details and a 3-business-day target for non-restricted evidence handover.

Key points in the appendix:
- Materiality threshold: incidents that materially impact confidentiality, integrity, or availability of customer data trigger the timeline.
- Interim notices: initial alert (within 24 hours) + daily status updates until the consolidated notification.
- Evidence handover: preserve-forensic-image, export logs (where lawful), and produce metadata/hashes; target 3 business days for data not subject to law enforcement/third-party holds, 5 business days where cross-border transfer or subprocessors require coordination.
- Subprocessor roster & liaison: Redwood will disclose the upstream subprocessor(s) involved in the event and provide a technical contact within 2 business days.

Two legal caveats we flagged: (a) in certain jurisdictions Redwood may be prevented from transferring raw data by local law — in that case Redwood will provide metadata/hashes and redacted exports and coordinate lawfully; (b) evidence requests that require full retention/forensic imaging may require a narrow scope and indemnity for cost depending on scale.

Attaching the appendix and redline now. If Finex is comfortable, Ben — please convert Redline into a tracked DPA attachment for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Privacy Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA-Finex-annotated-redline.pdf; forensic-evidence-spec.xlsx

From: procurement@finex.com <procurement@finex.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T17:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — notification timing + subprocessor cooperation questions

Marissa / Ben / Rishi — procurement and legal have reviewed the appendix and proposed redline. We can accept Option A with the 96-hour consolidated notification cap and the 3-business-day target for unrestricted evidence handover, plus the subprocessor roster/liaison commitments you outlined, subject to two small edits:

1) Add a clause that if Redwood must withhold raw exports for legal reasons, Redwood will provide a signed attestation from the subprocessor or local counsel describing the legal limitation within 5 business days.
2) Add a short SLA credit (one-time usage credit) tied to failure to meet the 96-hour consolidated notification in cases where the delay was within Redwood's control.

If you can accept those edits we will prepare the signature packet and routing for Q2. We appreciate the responsiveness.

Procurement
Finex Systems
